# Arkiv Chain Indexer

> A block explorer for an Arkiv chain: blocks, transactions, wallets, gas fees and storage rent, and the
> entities stored on chain with their typed attributes. Every page's filters and queries live in its URL, so
> a link reproduces exactly what the page shows.

Links are relative to this site's origin. Amounts are in wei. Arkiv transactions pay rent for storage
beside their gas fee; rent is burned and never counted as part of the fee. An entity whose expiry block is
18446744073709551615 (2^64 − 1) is permanent.

The entity explorer (`/entity-explorer`) lists the entities matching a query, as they are now. Its URL
parameters are `q` (the query, URL-encoded), `pageSize` (5, 10, 25, 50 or 100; default 50) and
`expiration` (`all`, or `soon` for entities expiring within 24 hours). A bare entity key or address in `q`
is read as `$key = key(0x...)` or `$owner = addr(0x...)`. Query syntax:

- A condition compares an attribute with a typed literal using `=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>` or `>=`:
  `status = str('open')`.
- Literals: `str('text')` (a quote inside is doubled: `str('it''s')`), `i32(-5)`, `u64(1200000)`,
  `u256(10)`, `dec(3.5)`, `addr(0x...)`, `key(0x...)`, `bytes32(0x...)`, and bare `true` / `false`.
- `name STARTSWITH str('prefix')`, `EXISTS(name)`, and `TYPEOF(name) = u64`.
- Combine with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` and parentheses. `&&` and `||` are not accepted.
- Entity fields: `$key`, `$owner`, `$creator`, `$createdAt` and `$expiresAt` (block numbers, as `u64(...)`).
- Entities written with a named schema carry the attribute `arkiv.schema`.
- Only indexed attributes match a condition; stored-only and `bytes` attributes never do.

Examples:

- `arkiv.schema = str('note')` →
  `/entity-explorer?q=arkiv.schema%20%3D%20str('note')`
- `$owner = addr(0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111) AND $createdAt > u64(100000)`, 10 per page →
  `/entity-explorer?q=%24owner%20%3D%20addr(0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111)%20AND%20%24createdAt%20%3E%20u64(100000)&pageSize=10`

Blocks, Transactions and Address pages take these URL parameters: `blockGt` and `blockLt` (block
numbers, exclusive), `dateGt` and `dateLt` (ISO-8601, e.g. `2026-10-30T12:00:00Z`), and `limit`.

## Pages

- [Home](/): search, latest blocks and latest transactions.
- [Search](/search?q=): what a block number, transaction hash, address or entity key refers to.
- [Blocks](/blocks): blocks with gas used, base fee, burned fees and rent. Example: `/blocks?blockGt=1000&blockLt=2000`.
- [Block](/block?block=): one block and its transactions; `block` is the block number.
- [Transactions](/transactions): transactions, newest first. Also takes `block` (one block), `address` (sent from or to it), and `page` with `limit` up to 1000.
- [Transaction](/tx/): `/tx/<hash>`; gas fee, rent, total cost and each entity operation (create, patch, extend, transfer, delete) with its attributes.
- [Wallets](/senders): the most active sender addresses.
- [Address](/address/): `/address/<address>`; a wallet's balance and transactions.
- [Entity explorer](/entity-explorer): query the entities stored on chain now; syntax above.
- [Entity](/entity/): `/entity/<entity key>`; an entity's current state and its full history of operations and rent.

## Optional

- [Statistics](/statistics): chain-wide totals of transactions, operations, fees, rent, entities and schemas.
- [Ranges](/ranges): block metrics aggregated per range; `rangeSize` is 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 500 or 1000 blocks.
- [Charts](/charts): block metrics over time; `blockStart`, `blockEnd`, `startDate`, and `xAxisMode` (`blocks` or `dates`).
- [Records](/records): the transactions with the most gas used, highest fee and highest effective gas price.
- [Activity](/activity): the senders using the most gas recently; `window` is `1h`, `6h` or `24h`.
